questions.question: What is the main advantage of the for-each over the classic for loop?
options: It lets you modify the array
It avoids index errors and is more readable
It lets you remove elements while iterating
explanations: Performance is similar; the advantage is safety and readability.
The for-each does NOT allow modifying the underlying array.
Correct. It hides the index, avoiding off-by-one errors and NullPointerException.
Removing elements in a for-each throws ConcurrentModificationException.
Using <= instead of < accesses index length, which does not exist.
The indices are 0,1,2; 3 is out of range.
Correct. When i == a.length (3), a[3] does not exist: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
The loop ends; the problem is the out-of-range access.

questions.question: In an int[][] m matrix, what does m[i].length represent in a nested for loop?
options: The number of columns in row i
explanations: m.length represents the number of rows.
Correct. m[i].length is the number of columns (elements) in row i.
It is not the total; that would be the sum across all rows.
The maximum index of row i is m[i].length - 1.
